football_evidence.question: Can Oregon keep Ohio State behind schedule?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Ohio State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.6 of the 6.1 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Ohio State has the ball (big plays through the air): Ohio State’s offense turns 15.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Oregon’s defense gives up explosive gains on 10.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Oregon has the ball (big plays through the air): Oregon’s offense turns 9.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Ohio State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Oregon has the ball (big plays on the ground): Oregon’s offense turns 3.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Ohio State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Ohio State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Ohio State’s offense averages 10.3 yards per pass attempt, and Oregon’s defense allows 6.6 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
contradicting: When Ohio State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Ohio State’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.6% of its dropbacks, and Oregon’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Oregon has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Oregon’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.5% of its dropbacks, and Ohio State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
